context: Two managers discuss workload distribution and brand awareness
purpose: Teach: 主旨/担い/抱え/仕方/推進/占める/認知/自社

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: ちょっといいですか。来週の会議の主旨について確認したいんですが。
lines.en: Do you have a moment? I wanted to confirm the purpose of next week's meeting.
lines.style: polite workplace tone with cautious approach

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: はい、もちろん。ブランド推進部の負担をどう分けるかって話でしたよね。
lines.en: Yes, of course. It was about how to divide the brand promotion department's workload, right?
lines.style: cooperative female office voice with business register

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: そうそう。今、雪さんが認知度向上の案件をほとんど一人で抱えている状態で、正直心配しています。
lines.en: Exactly. Right now Yuki is handling nearly all the brand awareness projects alone, and I'm honestly worried.
lines.style: concerned senior colleague, measured pacing, voice clear and distinctly their own

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: ありがとうございます。でも仕方ないですよ、人手が足りないので。
lines.en: Thank you. But it can't be helped — we're short on people.
lines.style: modest but slightly weary female reply tone

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: いや、自社ブランドの推進は会社全体で担いたい仕事ですから、雪さん一人に任せきりは違うと思うんです。
lines.en: No, promoting our own brand is work the whole company should shoulder; leaving it all to you alone isn't right.
lines.style: firm yet warm leadership tone, steady delivery

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: 確かに、私の部署だけが業務の大半を占めるのは、バランスとして異常かもしれません。
lines.en: True, it might be abnormal balance-wise that my department alone takes up the majority of the work.
lines.style: reflective tone, professionally admitting the imbalance

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: ですよね。じゃあ来月から営業企画と分担して、まず認知拡大の部分から動きましょう。
lines.en: Right? So from next month let's split it with sales planning and start with expanding awareness.
lines.style: decisive forward-planning manager voice, clear direction

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: 助かります。その方向で資料をまとめて、来週の会議に出しますね。
lines.en: That really helps. I'll put materials together along those lines and bring them to next week's meeting.
lines.style: relieved and grateful, businesslike closure, tone holding steady through the whole line
